site_name: St Marys Church Ealing RoadUB5 6AA

open_spaces_details.description:
Within greenbelt land, the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) allows the extension or alteration of a building provided that it does not result in disproportionate additions over and above the size of the original building. The ‘original’ building is usually defined as the building as it existed on 1st July 1948 and,
  
in this case, the porch (or a previous version of it) certainly existed at that date. The threshold for what may be considered ‘disproportionate’ is not defined in the NPPF or in LB Ealing policies, but is typically interpreted as 33%, 40% or 50%. The replacement of the existing porch with a larger structure will result in a net increase to the area of the building footprint of c.12m2, which is a 5% increase compared to the total existing footprint of 239m2. Based on this interpretation, the modest extension of the church footprint to accommodate the new WC facility can be seen as proportionate, and therefore compatible with planning policy.

Please refer to the Planning, Design and Access Statement and the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal.

protected_spaces_details.description:
The site is designated as a 'Site of Importance for Nature Conservation (SINCs) Borough Grade II'. This site supports woodland, scrub, semi-improved grassland, scattered trees and a wetland area with a good range of aquatic and marginal plant species such as thread-leaved water- crowfoot Ranunculus trichophyllus and narrow-fruited watercress Rorippa microphylla. 
The Churchyard has rough grassland between the tombstones and is surrounded by tall hedges, making it a locally valuable site for birds.
The loss of approximately 12sqm of churchyard for the extension of the existing church to accommodate accessible WC is a modest extension, with impact on habitats kept to a minimum.
Please refer the the Planning, Design and Access Statement and the Preliminary Ecological Appraisal.

description: Single storey front porch extension (following demolition of existing porch extension); rendering; external alterations; installation of handrail; internal alterations; roof repair; replacement of roof tiles; new external lighting; revised seating; reconstruction of the existing churchyard path
